## Stock Take Variance Calculator: Accuracy and Value
URL: https://tools.gantry.work/stock-take-variance-calculator.html
Summary: Free stock take variance calculator: paste system vs counted quantities for record accuracy, lines within tolerance, variance value and the top variances.
Answer: Inventory record accuracy = lines that match (within tolerance) ÷ lines counted × 100. Variance per line = counted − system quantity; variance value = variance × unit cost. Report the absolute variance as well as the net, because overs and shorts cancel in the net figure while both are real errors. Most operations aim for 95% or better within a 2% tolerance; below 85% the stock figure cannot be trusted for purchasing or costing. Checked 28 October 2026. Figures in S$; change the currency box for any other.
Q: How do you calculate stock take variance?
A: Variance per line is the counted quantity minus the system quantity; multiply by unit cost for the value. Sum the values for the net variance, and sum their absolute values for the absolute variance.
Q: What is a good inventory accuracy percentage?
A: Most operations target 95% or better within a small tolerance, and 98% or more for high-value or serialised items. Below 85% the records cannot support purchasing or costing decisions.
Q: Should I count the whole warehouse or cycle count?
A: Do a full count if accuracy is unknown or below 85%, then move to cycle counting so errors are caught near their cause. Many businesses keep one annual count for the audit plus weekly cycle counts.
Q: Why is my net variance small but my absolute variance large?
A: Because overs and shorts cancel. Two bins with +20 and −20 of the same item net to zero but mean the system cannot say where the stock is. Report both figures.

## What a System Project Really Consists Of: 9-Part Checklist
URL: https://tools.gantry.work/system-project-parts-checklist.html
Summary: The nine parts every ERP or system project has, whether or not they are in the proposal, and a check that shows which ones yours leaves out.
Q: What does an ERP project consist of?
A: Nine parts: software, implementation, changes for how your industry works, data migration and cleaning, links to other systems, training, your own people's time, support after go-live and a reserve for the unexpected. Software is only one of them.
Q: What is usually missing from an ERP proposal?
A: Data migration and cleaning, links to other systems, your own people's time, support after go-live and a reserve. These are the parts that stall projects later, so ask for each one to be included or excluded in writing, with who does it.
Q: Is the software the biggest part of an ERP project?
A: Usually not in effort. Implementation, data work, links and your own people's time decide the outcome far more than the software choice does.
Q: How much of our own staff time does an ERP project take?
A: More than most owners expect, and it is the part least often planned. Key users from finance, sales and operations spend time on workshops, cleaning data and testing for months; agree whose time, how many hours a week, and what they stop doing.

## Stalled ERP Project Rescue Checklist: 12 Checks
URL: https://tools.gantry.work/system-project-rescue-checklist.html
Summary: Your system project has been almost done for a year? Twelve checks that show where it is stuck, and the order to restart it. Free, printable.
Q: Why do ERP projects stall?
A: Usually not because of the software. They stall on the boring parts nobody inside the business owns: cleaning the master data, agreeing the opening balances, and testing the links to other systems. Scope creep keeps the team busy while those parts wait.
Q: How do I know if my system project has stalled?
A: Two or more of these: the go-live date has moved more than twice, opening balances still do not agree, staff run the old system or a spreadsheet alongside the new one, and meetings are about new features rather than the last open item.
Q: Should we change vendor to rescue a stalled project?
A: Not as the first step. First find which boring part has no owner. A new vendor inherits the same data, balances and links, so changing vendor without fixing ownership moves the problem rather than solving it.
Q: What is the first step to restart a stalled ERP project?
A: Name one owner inside the business who can decide, then give the data, the balances and the links an owner each, and freeze new features until the open items are closed.

## Three Way Match Example: PO, GRN, Invoice and a Live Checker
URL: https://tools.gantry.work/three-way-match-guide.html
Summary: Three-way matching with a worked example (100 ordered, 96 received, 100 invoiced), a live checker, a mismatch table and five steps for a small company.
Q: What is a three-way match, with an example?
A: It is a check that a supplier invoice agrees with the purchase order and the goods received note before it is paid. Example: 100 rolls ordered at S$12.00, 96 received, 100 invoiced. The invoice says S$1,200.00, the match says pay S$1,152.00 for the 96 that arrived and ask for a S$48.00 credit note.
Q: What is the difference between two-way and three-way matching?
A: Two-way matching compares the invoice with the purchase order only, so it checks price and ordered quantity. Three-way matching adds the goods received note, so it also checks that what was billed actually arrived. Use two-way for services and three-way for physical goods.
Q: Is a delivery order the same as a goods received note?
A: No. The delivery order is written by the supplier and says what they sent. The goods received note is your own record of what was counted and accepted. A small firm can use the supplier's delivery order as its receipt record, as long as its own receiver writes the counted quantity on it and signs.
Q: What tolerance should I set?
A: There is no official figure. It is a business decision about how small a difference is not worth a phone call. Start at zero for price so you see every difference for a month, then set a small percentage or dollar limit, write down who can approve above it, and review it once a year.
Q: What should I do when the invoice arrives before the goods?
A: Hold it unposted, or post it on hold, until the goods are counted in. Paying on the invoice alone is two-way matching by accident. If the supplier wants payment in advance, treat that as a deposit agreed on the purchase order, not as an early invoice.
Q: Does a small company really need three-way matching?
A: For anything bought for stock or for a job, yes, because that is where short deliveries and price creep hide. It does not need software to begin: a numbered purchase order, a counted and signed delivery order, and a rule that accounts sees both before paying will do.

## Free Timesheet Calculator with Overtime
URL: https://tools.gantry.work/timesheet-calculator.html
Summary: Free weekly timesheet calculator. Enter start and end times and breaks, get total hours in hours:minutes and decimal, overtime and pay. Overnight shifts, print and CSV export. No signup.
Q: How do I calculate hours worked?
A: Subtract the start time from the end time, then subtract unpaid breaks. 8:30am to 5:45pm with a 45-minute lunch is 9 hours 15 minutes minus 45 minutes, which is 8 hours 30 minutes, or 8.5 hours.
Q: How do I convert minutes to decimal hours?
A: Divide the minutes by 60. 15 minutes is 0.25 hours, 30 minutes is 0.5, 45 minutes is 0.75, and 20 minutes is 0.33.
Q: How is overtime calculated?
A: Hours above the overtime threshold are paid at a higher rate, usually 1.5 times the hourly rate. In Singapore, employees covered by Part IV of the Employment Act are paid at least 1.5 times for work beyond 44 hours a week; in the US the federal rule is over 40 hours a week.
Q: Does the calculator handle overnight shifts?
A: Yes. If the end time is earlier than the start time, the shift is treated as ending the next day, so 10pm to 6am counts as 8 hours.
Q: How many overtime hours are allowed in Singapore?
A: Up to 72 hours a month for employees under Part 4 of the Employment Act, unless the employer has an exemption from MOM. Overtime is paid at no less than 1.5 times the hourly basic rate.

## Before You Pay for WATI: WhatsApp Number Go-Live Checklist
URL: https://tools.gantry.work/wati-go-live-checklist.html
Summary: Eight things to have ready before you connect a business WhatsApp number to WATI: the number, Meta Business Manager access, website, display name and more. With a readiness score.
Q: Do I need a new number for WATI?
A: No. You can use a new number, move your current number after deleting the WhatsApp account on it, or use Coexistence to keep the WhatsApp Business app on the same number if you meet WATI's conditions.
Q: Can I keep the WhatsApp Business app and use WATI on the same number?
A: Yes, through Coexistence. WATI lists the conditions: the number is active in the WhatsApp Business app, the app is version 2.24.17 or later, you have a Facebook Business Page with admin access, and your country is supported.
Q: Do I need a website to connect a WhatsApp Business API number?
A: WATI asks for an active, public website showing your business name, products or services, contact details and address. You can begin with a Facebook Page or Instagram Business profile, but a website is needed for Facebook Business verification.
Q: Do I have to pay WATI before connecting my number?
A: Yes. WATI lists an active paid subscription as a requirement for connecting a business number. The free trial works without connecting it, by sending to your own WhatsApp number.
Q: Can I set up the WhatsApp number from my phone?
A: WATI's setup article asks for a laptop or desktop with Google Chrome, signed in to both Facebook and WATI.

## WATI for a Small Team in Singapore: the Plain Guide (2026)
URL: https://tools.gantry.work/wati-guide.html
Summary: What WATI is, who needs it and who does not, what a team of 3, 5 or 10 pays in Singapore, what the 7-day trial allows and what to have ready to go live.
Q: What is WATI used for?
A: WATI is a shared team inbox built on the official WhatsApp Business API. Several people can reply to customers from one business number, with chats assigned and tracked, and the same account can send broadcasts and run chatbots.
Q: How much does WATI cost in Singapore?
A: On WATI's pricing page on 10 November 2026, Growth was S$119 a month billed yearly (S$159 billed monthly) for 3 users, and Pro was S$329 a month billed yearly (S$429 billed monthly) for 5 users, with extra Pro users at S$35 each a month. Template message charges are added on top.
Q: Is WATI free to try?
A: Yes. WATI offers a 7-day free trial, and its trial article says no payment details are needed. During the trial, messages go to your own WhatsApp number only.
Q: Is WATI worth it for one person?
A: Usually not. One person replying can stay on the free WhatsApp Business app with quick replies, labels and an away message. A shared inbox starts to pay when two or more people share the same customer chats.
Q: Can I keep using the WhatsApp Business app with WATI?
A: Only through the Coexistence route, which keeps the WhatsApp Business app on the same number. WATI lists conditions for it, including a recent app version and a supported country. Otherwise the number has to come off the app first.

## WATI Pricing Singapore 2026: Cost for a Team of 3, 5 or 10
URL: https://tools.gantry.work/wati-pricing-singapore.html
Summary: WATI pricing in Singapore dollars: Growth S$119 and Pro S$329 a month billed yearly. Calculator for your team size, monthly or yearly billing, extra users and message charges.
Q: How much is WATI per month in Singapore?
A: On 10 November 2026 WATI's pricing page showed Growth at S$119 a month billed yearly or S$159 billed monthly, for 3 users, and Pro at S$329 a month billed yearly or S$429 billed monthly, for 5 users. Template message charges are added on top.
Q: Does WATI charge a setup fee?
A: WATI's pricing page lists zero setup fees and a 7-day free trial.
Q: Does WATI charge per message?
A: Template messages carry additional charges on every plan, and the rate depends on whether the message is marketing, utility or authentication. Check WATI's rate card for the current rates in your country.
Q: Can I add a fourth user on the WATI Growth plan?
A: No. Growth includes 3 users and has no option to add more. A fourth user needs the Pro plan, which includes 5 users and allows extra users at S$35 each a month.
Q: Is yearly billing cheaper than monthly?
A: Yes. On Growth the difference is S$40 a month, or S$480 over 12 months. On Pro it is S$100 a month, or S$1,200 over 12 months.

## WhatsApp Business API Cost Calculator 2026
URL: https://tools.gantry.work/whatsapp-api-cost-calculator.html
Summary: Free WhatsApp Business API cost calculator. Enter your chats, order updates and broadcasts to see Meta's monthly charges in Singapore, the October 2026 change and provider plans.
Q: How much does a WhatsApp Business API message cost in Singapore?
A: About S$0.0937 (US$0.0732) for a marketing message and S$0.0205 (US$0.016) for a utility or authentication message, per delivered message, for customers with Singapore numbers in 2026.
Q: Are replies to customers charged on the WhatsApp Business API?
A: Meta's developer documentation says that from 1 October 2026 replies inside the 24-hour customer service window are charged at the utility rate, while Meta's main pricing page still described them as free on 2 October 2026. The calculator lets you include or exclude that charge; check your first October invoice.
Q: Do I pay both Meta and a provider like WATI?
A: Yes. The provider charges a monthly plan for the shared inbox, broadcasts and automation, and Meta's message charges are passed on per message, sometimes with the provider's own markup.
Q: Which WhatsApp messages are free?
A: Conversations started from a click-to-WhatsApp ad or a Facebook Page button are free for 72 hours, and the free WhatsApp Business app has no message charges at all.

## Year-End Stock Take Checklist and Count Sheet
URL: https://tools.gantry.work/year-end-stock-take-checklist.html
Summary: A year-end stock take checklist: the count plan from two weeks out, a freeze and cut-off note, a count sheet and the variance in dollars. Free PDF.
Q: What should a year-end stock take checklist include?
A: Four stages. Two weeks before: fix the date, clear the returns shelf, post paperwork and list stock held outside. One week before: label every location, print count sheets with no system quantities and pair the counters. On the day: freeze movement, write down the cut-off numbers and count every location. After: work out the variance in dollars and adjust the records once, with one approver.
Q: Why should the count sheet not show the system quantity?
A: Because a counter who sees 120 on the sheet tends to find 120. A sheet with no system quantity makes the counter write what is on the shelf. The system quantity is added later, by someone who did not count, on a separate comparison list.
Q: What is a stock take cut-off?
A: It is the line between this period and the next. Before the first count, write down the last goods receipt, delivery order, sales invoice and transfer or adjustment numbers. Anything with a higher number belongs to the next period.
Q: How do I calculate stock take variance in dollars?
A: For each line, take the counted quantity minus the system quantity and multiply by the unit cost. Total the shorts and the overs separately, as well as the net. In the example on this page the shorts are S$1,897, the overs S$440 and the net S$1,457, which is 4.5% of the S$32,550 in the records.
Q: What are the most common causes of a short stock count?
A: In my experience, three. Paperwork and stock out of step, such as a delivery that was not recorded. A wrong unit or a missed place, such as boxes counted as pieces or stock held at a forwarder. And stock used without an entry: samples, replacements and damaged goods thrown away. Check these three before you assume theft.
Q: When should I fix the date for a December 2026 stock count?
A: Now. Christmas Day (25 December 2026) and New Year's Day (1 January 2027) both fall on a Friday, according to the Ministry of Manpower public holidays page read on 11 November 2026. Tell sales, purchasing and the warehouse two weeks before the count, and send the freeze note two working days before.
Q: Is there a free stock take template in Excel?
A: The count sheet on this page prints as a template: item, location, a blank count box and no system quantity. If you keep the count in Excel, use the same columns plus the system quantity on a separate hidden sheet, and paste both into the stock take variance calculator to get accuracy and the variance in dollars.
